messages:
Ashley (Engineering): Hey People Ops — quick question. I'm switching from Dental PPO to HMO during open enrollment. Do I need to get separate signed consent/acknowledgement from my spouse and children, or can I just update the coverage on my end? Also, if we switch to HMO, do dependents need to select a primary dentist immediately? Thanks!

Maria (People Ops): Short answer: you don't need separate signature for adults unless they're enrolling themselves. For spouse and minor children, your update is sufficient but we do need proof of relationship for new dependents. If you're only changing plan for already-covered dependents, no extra docs. :sparkles:

Kevin (Benefits): Add: HMO usually requires selecting a PCP for each enrollee. The portal will prompt you to pick a primary dentist (we call it 'Primary Care Dentist' in the system) for each covered person. If you skip it, the carrier may assign one automatically which can affect network coverage.

Ashley (Engineering): Ah — thanks. What about my partner being on a separate plan currently at their employer? They'd be switching over to mine mid-year. Is that a qualifying life event or does it need to wait for open enrollment?

Maria (People Ops): Losing other coverage is a SEP — if their employer plan ends, you have 30 days to add them. If it's voluntary, they'd need to drop at same time as joining. We can help document the SEP. Please DM me the date their coverage ends.

Lia (People Ops): Filing steps: 1) Go to Benefits Portal -> 'Report a Qualifying Event' 2) Upload proof (letter from their employer or termination of coverage) 3) Pick plan and hit 'Submit'. If you need us to pre-fill the SEP form, reply here and @Maria will help.

HR-Bot: Reminder: If adding dependents mid-year, documentation must be uploaded within 30 days of event per policy: https://redwood.hr/policy/dependent-enrollment (auto-reminder in 3 days).

Kevin (Benefits): For dental HMO specifically, carriers sometimes ask for dependent identification (e.g., SSN or passport for non-US docs). If spouse is international and has no SSN, send passport + marriage certificate. We'll route to carrier.

Ashley (Engineering): This is great — one more: do minor kids need a signed parental consent form to be added? They are minors so I'm assuming no.

Maria (People Ops): Correct, minors are added by the enrolling parent/guardian. If custody is split we might need custody docs. Otherwise, upload birth certificate and you're good. I'll drop the quick checklist: 

Maria (People Ops): ```Checklist:
- Birth certificate(s) for each child
- Marriage certificate for spouse (if applicable)
- Proof of loss of other coverage (for SEP)
- ID (SSN or passport) for spouse if requested by carrier
- Select primary dentist(s) in portal
```

Ashley (Engineering): Thanks all! I'll upload docs today. @Lia if you can pre-fill SEP form that'd be awesome.

Lia (People Ops): On it — DM me the termination date and spouse name. I'll send a prefilled pdf.
